items.title: Zetrix AI sinks to five sen as RM2bil sukuk covenant breach looms
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Zetrix AI Bhd shares hit a fresh low of five sen on Friday as the embattled technology company faces a potential breach of its RM2 billion sukuk covenant, adding to a string of setbacks in recent months. At 5.5 sen, Zetrix AI had a market capitalisation of about RM444.33 million. The latest sell-off came after Zetrix AI disclosed that its managing director, Wong Thean Soon, was no longer the company's single largest shareholder following forced share sales by banks.

items.title: Tuanku Muhriz has stern words with Negri MB
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A video showing Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir having a stern word with Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim amid the state's constitutional crisis has gone viral. Ismail is seen acknowledging Tuanku Muhriz and paying homage to the ruler. A week later, Tuanku Muhriz revoked the appointments of all 10 state executive councillors.

items.title: PeKa B40 to be rebranded as PeKa Sihat
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The cabinet has agreed to rebrand the PeKa B40 programme as PeKa Sihat, with measures being drawn up to improve its effectiveness and ease congestion at public health clinics. Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the Health Ministry was coordinating several proposed changes, including the use of premises and clinics participating in the programme. "The cabinet agreed to amend the Health Ministry's PeKa B40 programme, taking into account its effectiveness in addressing non-communicable diseases.

items.title: Azalina to hold more talks with parliamentary committee on AG-Public Prosecutor Separation Bill
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said has been directed to hold further discussions with the Parliamentary Special Select Committee on the proposed constitutional amendments to separate the roles of the Attorney-General (A-G) and Public Prosecutor (PP). Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim issued the directive following several matters raised by the Malay Rulers during the Conference of Rulers on the proposed amendments. "The prime minister has directed Azalina to hold engagement sessions and discussions with the Parliamentary Special Select Committee, which prepared the draft constitutional amendments.

items.title: Heavy downpour triggers flash floods across Kuching, roads and Sarawak Plaza basement swamped
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 16 — Several areas in Kuching were hit by flash floods following heavy rain this afternoon. Flooding was reported at Sarawak Plaza, the Mile 3 underpass, Jalan Tun Jugah and Jalan Batu Lintang after the rain began at around 1.30pm. As of 2.45pm, the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) had forecast thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in several parts of Sarawak until 7pm.

items.title: Miti to expand markets, strengthen Malaysia's export performance under 2027 Budget
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry (Miti) will continue to expand and strengthen Malaysia's export markets through initiatives under the 2027 Budget. Deputy Minister Sim Tze Tzin said Miti, through the Malaysia External Trade Development Corporation, would lead export-strengthening initiatives through the RM60 million Export Capacity Building Programme and the RM50 million Export Strengthening and Market Diversification Fund. The initiatives would also be supported by RM1 billion in financing facilities from Bank Pembangunan Malaysia Bhd and RM10 million through EXIM Bank.

items.title: ‘Until he retracts, go away’: Tuanku Muhriz rebukes Negeri Sembilan MB in public
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 16 — The Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, publicly reprimanded Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim as the state’s constitutional crisis drags on. Videos circulating on social media show the ruler telling a group of people that Ismail had written to the Keeper of the Rulers’ Seal to say that Tuanku Muhriz was no longer the state’s Yang Dipertuan Besar. A visibly angry Tuanku Muhriz then asked why the menteri besar wanted an audience with him.

items.title: Malaysia’s fury rises as Indonesian haze shuts schools, blankets region, and sparks calls for accountability
items.summary: Indonesian wildfire haze has caused a regional pollution crisis and prompted growing frustration in neighbours, including Malaysia. “Malaysia and Indonesia are close neighbours, but that relationship must also come with responsibility,” Malaysian parliamentarian Syerleena Abdul Rashid told AFP. she said.

items.title: Duta Enclave: Govt overpaid up to RM500,000 in land compensation, court told
items.summary: Government-appointed valuer Tan Tat Khuan said his assessment showed that the government had overpaid by between RM400,000 and RM500,000 when it compensated the company for the land acquired in 1956. He said his valuation placed the compensation at between RM875,000 and RM985,000, compared with the approximately RM1.39 million previously paid by the government. Tan said his first valuation placed the land's value at RM875,000, while the second put it at RM985,000.

items.title: Malaysia needs to upskill, digitalise MSMEs to boost growth, wages
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia needs to accelerate the upskilling and digitalisation of micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) to strengthen their contribution to economic growth and ensure workers benefit more from rising productivity, said Nottingham University Malaysia economist Dr Tan Shih-Ming. "So Malaysia has to find ways of upskilling and digitalising MSMEs moving forward so that they could actually contribute to larger economic growth for the country as a result," he said in an interview on Bernama World's programme, "Budget 2027: Malaysia's Growth and Global Competitiveness". Tan said Malaysia's economic growth was expected to moderate after this year's strong export performance, particularly in artificial intelligence (AI), semiconductors and electrical and electronics (E&E), which contributed to a 30 per cent increase in exports.

items.title: Khazanah and PNB channelled nearly RM40m into FashionValet in 2018, court hears in Vivy Yusof trial
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 16 — The Sessions Court here was told today that local fashion company, Fashion Valet Sdn Bhd (Fashion Valet), received investment funds totalling nearly RM40 million from Khazanah Nasional Berhad (Khazanah) and Permodalan Nasional Berhad (PNB) eight years ago. Tay Lay Hong, 54, a banking services manager at the Bukit Damansara branch of Public Bank, said the funds were deposited into a Public Bank account belonging to Fashion Valet through four separate transactions between March and December 2018. Tay also confirmed that a sum of RM11 million was withdrawn from Fashion Valet’s bank account on August 21, 2018, via an online ‘bulk payment’ transaction.

items.title: Singapore and China can drive regional growth in digital, green sectors
items.summary: Singapore Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong, who is also Trade and Industry Minister, said both countries could build on decades of cooperation to strengthen capabilities in Singapore and across Asean. "Singapore and China have spent decades building trust through mutually beneficial cooperation. We should now draw on that trust to build capabilities in Singapore and across Asean," he said.

items.title: Seven foreigners claim trial over Forest City crypto scam
items.summary: The accused — Hong Wei Xian, 25; Zhou Fu, 22; Chen Lu, 23; Yuan Shuping, 29; Li Yi, 30; Wang Tengfei, 30; and Chen Xiaojia, 33 — pleaded not guilty after the charges were read to them in Mandarin before magistrate Atifah Hazimah Wahab. Deputy public prosecutor Sarah Siti Aisyah Mustapha Kamal proposed bail of RM15,000 for each accused, with two local sureties. Lawyer Pang Yong Tong, representing Hong, Zhou and Chen Lu, also sought lower bail, citing the student status of three of the accused and their residence at Forest City.

items.title: Malaysian businesses, umrah agencies cautious after Riyadh airport attack
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian businesses and umrah agencies have adopted a cautious approach to their operations in the Middle East amid security concerns following a deadly attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh last week. The Malaysia External Trade Development Corporation (Matrade) said Malaysian companies in the retail and consumer sectors in the region had adopted measures to adapt to the current situation. Meanwhile, Pertubuhan Agensi Umrah dan Haji Sarawak (Suha) chairman Ruzaiman Ghazalee said some airlines had cancelled umrah flights before the Riyadh airport attack, prompting several umrah agencies in Sarawak to switch to other airlines.

items.title: Sarawak helicopter crash: Review needed for rescue, firefighting operations at Long Lellang
items.summary: The Air Accidents Investigation Bureau (AAIB), however, noted that the Rela personnel were not wearing firefighting personal protective equipment (PPEs). "Rescue and firefighting duties at the airstrip had been assigned to Aviation Security (Avsec) Rela personnel acting as auxiliary rescue and firefighting personnel. However, no dedicated rescue and firefighting personnel were stationed at the STOLport," it said.

items.title: AAIB releases preliminary report on Long Lellang helicopter crash that killed five
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 16 — The Air Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) has published its preliminary report into the September 8 crash of a Flying Doctor Service helicopter at the Long Lellang STOLport in Miri, Sarawak, which killed a pilot and four passengers. The Transport Ministry said the Bolkow BO105 S helicopter, registered 9M-LLF and operated by Layang-Layang Aerospace Sdn Bhd, was on a scheduled Flying Doctor Service flight from Selungo to the Long Lellang STOLport at the time of the accident. It said the report compiles the factual information identified at the early stage of the investigation, in line with the government’s commitment to transparency and accountability.

items.title: Cable thief caught red-handed along NKVE
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A cable thief has been arrested following a joint operation by Plus Malaysia Bhd (Plus) personnel and police along the New Klang Valley Expressway (NKVE). Plus said the arrest was made during a recent operation to curb the theft and destruction of critical highway infrastructure. "Through our continued commitment, the Plus team, in cooperation with police, successfully arrested a suspect involved in cable theft activities along the NKVE during a recent operation," it said.

items.title: Sarawak helicopter crash: Pilot medically fit, aircraft was airworthy, weather conditions good
items.summary: The Air Accidents Investigation Bureau (AAIB) in its preliminary report found that 30-year-old Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham, from Seremban, had 1,825.5 flight hours under his belt, including 915 hours and 50 minutes on the Bo-105 helicopter type. The AAIB report said the Zainol had logged 81 hours and 48 minutes of flying time in the 90 days before the Sept 8 crash, while his rest period before the final flight was 22 hours. "He held a valid Commercial Pilot Licence (Helicopter), with an aircraft rating for the Bo-105, and his licence was valid until Jan 31, 2027.

items.title: Sarawak gives RM100,000 each to families of Flying Doctor Service crash victims
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 16 — The Sarawak state government has contributed RM100,000 to each of the families of the five victims of the Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter crash in Long Lellang, Baram, which occurred on September 8. Additionally, educational assistance is being provided through Yayasan Sarawak (Sarawak Foundation) to help ease the burden on the victims’ families, specifically by ensuring the continuity of their children’s education. The contributions were presented by Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg to the next-of-kin of the five victims during a handover ceremony held at the Sarawak State Legislative Assembly complex today.

items.title: Sarawak helicopter crash: Preliminary report released, no cause found yet
items.summary: The preliminary report released by the Air Accidents Investigation Bureau (AAIB) states the safety investigation remained ongoing, with the available factual data still only at a preliminary stage. "Continuous fact-finding regarding flight operations, standard operating practices, and helicopter maintenance history will provide the necessary evidence to validate system defences and evaluate any latent conditions," the report read. "The recovered powerplant components were subsequently transported to the engine manufacturer's facility for further examination and analysis," it said.

items.title: Protecting young lungs: Why proper masks matter during haze
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Parents should not underestimate the health risks posed by prolonged exposure to haze, particularly its potential impact on children's lung development. Universiti Teknologi Mara (UiTM) Faculty of Health Sciences senior lecturer Dr Noor Haziqah Kamaludin said children's respiratory systems continued to develop into their early 20s, making them more vulnerable to air pollution. She said children breathed faster to meet their bodies' higher oxygen demands.

items.title: Lawyers urge public to avoid speculation as Zara Qairina inquest heads to January ruling
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Oct 16 — Lawyers involved in the inquest into the death of Zara Qairina Mahathir have urged the public to avoid speculation and allow the judicial process to take its course following the conclusion of witness testimonies. Lawyer Joan Goh, who represents one of the teenagers accused in the bullying case involving the Form One student, said she hoped the evidence presented during the inquest had been addressed comprehensively. “The coroner also sought feedback and recommendations from all parties on improving future inquest proceedings, including school safety and investigation procedures,” he said.

items.title: Fashion Valet received nearly RM40mil from Khazanah, PNB in 2018, court told
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Sessions Court was told today that Fashion Valet Sdn Bhd received nearly RM40 million in investment funds from Khazanah Nasional Bhd (Khazanah) and Permodalan Nasional Bhd (PNB) in 2018. "An examination of the company's bank statements showed that Khazanah transferred RM7.84 million on March 23, 2018, and RM11.74 million on March 26, 2018. "PNB recorded transfers of RM11.95 million on June 4, 2018, and RM8.36 million on Dec 20, 2018," he said.

items.title: [UPDATED]: Anwar to discuss haze at special meeting on Monday
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim will chair a special meeting on Monday to discuss several issues, including the haze currently affecting the country. Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the High-Level Committee (HLC) meeting on National Disaster Management would, among others, focus on the need for better coordination among ministries to address the haze impact. "The Education Ministry and Health Ministry had informed the cabinet that existing guidelines to address the haze were based on the National Haze Action Plan, which was currently in force.

items.title: Police confirm AKPS officer killed in KLIA quarters domestic dispute, knife seized, husband remanded
items.summary: Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said police received a report regarding the incident at about 9.30pm after a man surrendered himself at the Bandar Baru Salak Tinggi Police Station in Sepang, Selangor, and reported his wife’s death at their residence. Acting on the information, a police team was dispatched to the scene, where they found a woman, in her 30s, unconscious. He said initial investigations by the Negeri Sembilan D10 Forensic Division found that the victim sustained injuries suspected to be from being stabbed, while a knife along with several other pieces of evidence were also seized to assist in the investigation.

items.title: [UPDATED] No Malaysian plantation firms linked to Indonesia forest fires, says Fahmi
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: No Malaysian plantation companies with oil palm concessions in Indonesia have been found to be involved in forest fires linked to the haze. Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said cross-checks with Malaysian companies showed that most of the fires observed had occurred outside concessions owned by Malaysian firms. Fahmi said the Malaysian Palm Oil Board would continue to engage with Malaysian plantation companies operating in Indonesia.

items.title: Tougher penalties for illegal racing, tonto activities take effect today
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Tougher penalties for illegal racing, tonto (lookout) activities and vehicle document forgery took effect today under amendments to the Road Transport Act, the Transport Ministry said. Section 110B addresses tonto activities, which involve obstructing enforcement operations, including following enforcement vehicles and leaking operational information to help others evade legal action. Amendments to Section 53B strengthen the accountability of registered vehicle owners for offences detected by enforcement cameras, including automated enforcement systems.

items.title: Four men arrested over Pekan Forest Reserve fire
items.summary: PEKAN: Police have detained four men suspected of causing a large-scale fire at the Pekan Forest Reserve here on Monday. He said they were detained to assist in investigations into the fire at a peat swamp forest adjacent to their residential area. Meanwhile, Pahang Forestry Department deputy director (Development) Harry Yong said the fire at the Pekan Forest Reserve last week had destroyed more than 80 hectares of peat swamp forest.

items.title: Bersama member wants action against those spreading khalwat allegations
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A Parti Bersama Malaysia (Bersama) member wants the party to take civil legal action and lodge a police report against those accused of spreading defamatory allegations linking a senior party leader to a khalwat arrest case. Bersama member for Wangsa Maju, Ahmad Fariz Abdullah, said legal action should be initiated against those who originated and spread the allegations, including social media account owners and news portals involved. "Today, I express my anger and condemn the irresponsible actions of any party attempting to link a senior party leader to a khalwat arrest case.

items.title: Sarawak gives RM100,000 to families of Long Lellang helicopter crash victims
items.summary: KUCHING: The Sarawak government has contributed RM100,000 to each of the five families of those killed in the Sept 8 Flying Doctor Service helicopter crash in Long Lellang, Baram. Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg presented the contributions to the victims' next-of-kin at a handover ceremony at the Sarawak State Assembly complex today. On Sept 8, a BO-105 helicopter carrying five people, including the pilot, crashed near the Short Take-Off and Landing Port (STOLport) in Long Lellang.

items.title: Malaysian Bar calls for natural justice in Negri Sembilan crisis
items.summary: Its president, Anand Raj, said this included any moves allegedly aimed at removing the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir. He said any attempt to compel Tuanku Muhriz to stop performing his duties or abdicate must comply with Article X(1) of the Laws of the Constitution of Negri Sembilan 1959. "The basis for the state executive council's action at the time in allegedly suspending the State Secretary and the State Legal Adviser on Sept 22 also raises questions," he said.

items.title: Japan's Nikkei snaps six-day losing streak as AI shares rebound
items.summary: The Nikkei rose 1.39 per cent to 65,324.29 after a near five per cent drop in the previous session. The broader Topix rose 1.67 per cent to 4,066 but fell 0.95 per cent for the week. In Japan, chip-making equipment maker Tokyo Electron rose 2.56 per cent, memory chip maker Kioxia gained 3.84 per cent and technology investor SoftBank Group rose 1.9 per cent.

items.title: Kelantan KPDN probes subsidised cooking oil supply chain
items.summary: KOTA BARU: The Kelantan Ministry of Domestic Trade and Cost of Living (KPDN) is conducting further investigations to determine whether other parties were involved in the misappropriation of subsidised cooking oil, following the seizure of 4,127 kilogrammes of the controlled item in Kampung Chetok, Pasir Mas, yesterday. Kelantan KPDN director Hanif Yusabra Yusuf said the investigation aims to uncover potential illicit activities involving the misappropriation of subsidised controlled goods. During the operation part of 'Ops Tiris 4.0 (Integrated) carried out at 8 pm, the Kelantan KPDN seized subsidised cooking oil valued at RM11,053.50, along with five vehicles, bringing the total value of the seizure to RM138,053.50.

items.title: PetroChina to restart part of shuttered Dalian refinery in November, sources say
items.summary: SINGAPORE: PetroChina is preparing to restart a mothballed crude oil processing unit in northeast China next month to replenish domestic fuel stocks until a replacement refinery is constructed, according to multiple industry and trade sources. PetroChina previously planned to restart a 200,000 bpd crude distillation unit (CDU) at Dalian in mid-2026, but the plan was held back as the US-Israeli war with Iran disrupted crude supplies and sent prices surging. The plan to restart the CDU gained traction in recent months as China has faced depleted crude and fuel stocks after months of reduced crude imports and refining output because of the supply disruptions.

items.title: Family stunned by suspect's call informing them of Customs officer's death
items.summary: TUMPAT: The family of a 35-year-old Customs officer who was allegedly murdered by her husband at their home in the Kuala Lumpur International Airport quarters yesterday, were left stunned when the suspect told them she was dead. The victim's elder brother, Hazwan Ibrahim, 38, said the suspect told him his youngest sister, Nor Hazwani Ibrahim, had died and that he would surrender to police. Police confirmed yesterday that Nor Hazwani was found murdered at the KLIA quarters in Jalan Kuarters KLIA in Nilai.

items.title: 14 arrested, 10 test positive for drugs in Temerloh R&R operation
items.summary: TEMERLOH: Fourteen people were arrested, including 10 men who tested positive for methamphetamine, during an integrated multi-agency operation at the Temerloh Rest and Recreation (R&R) stop along the East Coast Expressway last night. A total of 139 summonses were also issued during the operation. District police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Nasyim Bahron said three men were arrested by the Narcotics Crime Investigation Department after testing positive for methamphetamine.

items.title: China central bank chief touted yuan assets to investors, Bloomberg News reports
items.summary: BEIJING: China's central bank governor Pan Gongsheng touted yuan assets to investors at a closed-door event in Bangkok and outlined plans to expand their role in global markets, Bloomberg News said on Friday, citing some who attended. Pan highlighted the resilience of Chinese assets, particularly government bonds, and the diversification they can bring to investment portfolios, the report said. Pan cited data showing a portfolio of 80 per cent yuan bonds and 20 per cent Chinese equities delivered a larger annual return over two decades than a global asset portfolio, the report added.

items.title: UN report warns global biodiversity action off track, urges implementation
items.summary: YEREVAN (Armenia): UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres on Thursday launched the first global assessment report on the implementation of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, warning that global efforts remain off track to meet the 2030 targets despite widespread national commitments. According to the report, nearly 90 per cent of the CBD's 196 Parties have established national biodiversity targets, close to 60 per cent have developed national biodiversity strategies and action plans, and over 70 per cent have submitted national reports. None of the 23 global targets presents a fully positive picture, and fewer than half of the national targets assessed by Parties are currently on track, the report found.

items.title: China agrees in principle to Malaysia’s proposal for world TVET council, says Zahid
items.summary: TIANJIN, Oct 16 — China has agreed in principle to Malaysia’s proposal to establish a World Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) Council, said Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi. He noted that the proposal to establish the World TVET Council, with China acting as the permanent secretariat, was formally presented during his keynote address at the World Technical and Vocational Education and Training Development Conference 2026 (WVTEDC 2026) here today. In terms of principle, Deputy Prime Minister Ding and China’s Minister of Education have agreed,” he said during a press conference following the event.

items.title: Tuanku Muhriz bestows state honours on three Undangs and their consorts
items.summary: The Negeri Sembilan State Secretary’s Office said in a statement today that the three Undangs - Datuk Klana Petra Muhammad Faris Johari of Luak Sungei Ujong, Datuk Mendika Menteri Akhirulzaman Datuk Azrin Khairi of Luak Jelebu and Datuk Sedia Raja Hassan Ab Hamid of Luak Rembau — were conferred the Darjah Tertinggi Negeri Sembilan (DTNS). Also present at the ceremony were the Tunku Ampuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Aishah Rohani Tengku Besar Mahmud, Tunku Besar Seri Menanti Tunku Ali Redhauddin Tuanku Muhriz, and Tunku Panglima Besar Tunku Zain Al-‘Abidin. Other attendees included State Secretary Datuk Mohd Zafir Ibrahim, State Legal Adviser Datuk Muzalmah Mustapha Kamal and State Financial Officer Datuk Masri Razali.

items.title: PKR to contest nine Melaka seats, Pakatan to unveil full line-up on Oct 24
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 16 — PKR will contest nine state seats under Pakatan Harapan (PH) in the upcoming Melaka state election on November 14, party secretary-general Datuk Fuziah Salleh said. She said the names of PKR candidates, together with those from other PH component parties, would be officially announced by coalition chairman Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim on October 24. Fuziah said the announcement would be made during the launch of the PH election machinery at the parking lot of Hang Jebat Stadium in Melaka at 8pm.

items.title: New road transport law takes effect, illegal street racing now a specific offence
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 16 — The Road Transport (Amendment) Act 2026, which amends the Road Transport Act 1987 (Act 333), came into force today, introducing new provisions to curb illegal street racing and ‘tonto’ syndicate activities, as well as strengthen enforcement and the digitalisation of Road Transport Department (JPJ) services. The Transport Ministry (MOT) said the Act, which contains 42 amendment clauses, was part of the government’s efforts to improve road safety, strengthen enforcement and modernise JPJ service delivery. MOT said the Act also introduces Section 110B to address ‘tonto’ syndicate activities that obstruct or interfere with enforcement operations, including tailing enforcement vehicles and relaying information about operations.

items.title: School bus operators told to update driver records by Oct 30 for RM1,000 aid before Deepavali
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 16 — All school bus owners and operators have been urged to update their drivers’ details from today until October 30 to facilitate the disbursement of RM1,000 in special financial assistance. The required information includes each driver’s current name, address, telephone number, valid driving and Public Service Vehicle (PSV) licences, and bank account number for payment. The agency said it had also engaged with the Federation of Malaysian School Bus Associations and the Kuala Lumpur and Selangor School Bus Operators Association to ensure an orderly and accurate eligibility verification and payment process.

items.title: Sarawak says RM1.5b interim grant not final, pushes for clear constitutional formula
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 16 — The increase in the interim payment of the special grant to Sarawak to RM1.5 billion does not constitute a definitive solution, said Deputy Minister in the Sarawak Premier’s Department (Law, MA63 and State-Federal Relations) Datuk Sharifah Hasidah Sayeed Aman Ghazali. She stressed that the Sarawak government would continue to push for a clear and consistent formula to be established under Article 112D of the Federal Constitution. “For a long-term solution, the Sarawak government has proposed that a clear and consistent formula be established to determine the rate of the special grant.

items.title: Sitiawan fire claims lives of two teenage sisters, homes and vehicles gutted in morning inferno
items.summary: IPOH, Oct 16 — Two sisters were killed after being trapped in a fire that destroyed two adjoining double-storey houses in Kampung Koh, near Sitiawan, today. Perak Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) director Datuk Sayani Saidon said the two sisters were aged 15 and 18. “They found the blaze involved two adjoining Class C houses measuring 40ft by 70ft each, which were almost 90 per cent destroyed, with the two sisters trapped inside,” she said in a statement today, adding that the fire also destroyed four vehicles and a motorcycle.

items.title: Budget 2027 debate dominates Dewan Rakyat as MPs tackle haze, health and school safety
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 16 — Debate on the Supply (Budget) Bill 2027 was the main focus of the Dewan Rakyat in the second week of the Third Meeting of the Fifth Session of the 15th Parliament, alongside current issues such as haze, health, education and school safety, as well as the cost of living. A total of 75 government and opposition Members of Parliament (MPs) debated the Supply Bill 2027 at the policy stage over four days, beginning Monday (Oct 12), following the tabling of Budget 2027 by Prime Minister and Finance Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim on October 9. During the oral question-and-answer session, Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the procurement of 400 new ambulances would enhance emergency response capabilities for critical cases.

items.title: Jais confirms two arrests in alleged khalwat case involving public figure
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Oct 16 — The Selangor Islamic Religious Department (Jais) has confirmed the arrest of two people to assist investigations into an alleged khalwat case involving a public figure in Petaling Jaya yesterday, Sinar Harian reported. Jais director Datuk Mohd Shahzihan Ahmad said the arrests were made at about 6pm over suspected offences under Section 29 of the Syariah Criminal Offences (Selangor) Enactment 1995. The claims sparked speculation before Jais confirmed the arrests.

items.title: Johor’s Pasir Gudang records API 207, highest nationwide as 30 areas hit unhealthy levels
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 16 — Pasir Gudang in Johor recorded a very unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) reading of 207, the highest in the country, while 30 other areas recorded unhealthy readings as of 9am today. In Kuala Lumpur, Batu Muda recorded an API reading of 170 and Cheras 168, while Putrajaya registered 174. Meanwhile, 37 areas recorded moderate API readings.

items.title: Coroner’s Court sets Jan 15, 2027 for verdict in Zara Qairina inquest
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Oct 16 — The Coroner’s Court here has set January 15 next year to deliver its decision on the inquest into the death of Zara Qairina Mahathir. Coroner Amir Shah Amri Hassan fixed the date today following discussions with all parties involved in the inquest. Amir Shah also said that the court had fixed January 8, 2027, for the clarification of the submissions.

items.title: Sarawak formulates proposals to improve Flying Doctor Service, strengthen Medevac and rural health delivery
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 16 — Sarawak is exploring ways to improve healthcare delivery to remote communities following the suspension of its Flying Doctor Service (FDS) after a helicopter crash in Long Lellang, Baram, that claimed five lives on September 8. Deputy Minister of Public Health, Housing and Local Government Datuk Michael Tiang said alternative healthcare delivery methods would be used temporarily while the government formulates proposals to improve the service’s safety and effectiveness. “The government will continue to evaluate and improve the methods of delivering healthcare services to rural areas, taking into account aspects of safety, effectiveness and service continuity, to ensure that rural communities continue to have access to the necessary healthcare services,” he said.

items.title: Sarawak state assembly suspends DAP’s Chong Chieng Jen over offensive language, unverified claims in Budget debate
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 16 — Chong Chieng Jen (DAP-Padungan) has been suspended for the remainder of the State Legislative Assembly (DUN) sitting for misleading the House and making unsubstantiated allegations while debating the 2027 Sarawak Budget. He said the DAP Sarawak chairman had used offensive and insulting language against members of the House, and had imputed improper motives to other members or made statements or allegations which the said member was not prepared to substantiate. Every member must observe the Standing Orders, respect the authority of the Chair, and exercise care in making statements and allegations in this House,” he said.

items.title: MPs demand tougher Asean haze response, call for disaster fund and stricter enforcement
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 16 — Bagan MP Lim Guan Eng has proposed the establishment of a permanent Asean task force to tackle the transboundary haze crisis, in cooperation with Singapore, the Philippines, and Indonesia. He said if Indonesia continues to reject the task force over sovereignty concerns, Malaysia would have no choice but to initiate legal action to claim compensation. “This haze is a man-made disaster.

items.title: Man with 33 criminal, drug records arrested over glue tin attack on elderly man in Segamat
items.summary: SEGAMAT, Oct 16 — A 70-year-old man sustained a forehead injury after he was allegedly struck with a tin of glue by a man outside a business premises in Jalan Mohd Yusof, Kampung Abdullah yesterday, Sinar Harian reported. Segamat district police chief Superintendent Mohd Jumazanzahir Chek Ismail said preliminary investigations found that the incident occurred after the victim confronted the suspect for allegedly making a commotion outside the premises. Police subsequently arrested a 40-year-old local man believed to be involved in the incident following intelligence gathered by the Segamat district police headquarters’ Criminal Investigation Division.

items.title: School assessment postponed as haze sparks MOE move to prioritise student health and safety
items.summary: According to the Ministry, as the UASA is a school-based assessment, schools are granted the flexibility to reschedule the assessment dates. MOE also acknowledged the dilemma faced by parents and guardians, who must balance their children’s health with the need to ensure they do not miss the assessment. “MOE understands the dilemma faced by parents.

items.title: Rapid KL: Cable theft attempt halts power on Kajang Line for an hour, police report lodged
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 16 — An attempted cable theft between the Phileo Damansara and Pusat Bandar Damansara stations disrupted MRT Kajang Line services early this morning. Rapid KL said the incident was detected at 5.30am, following an intrusion into the track area. Rapid KL said alternative train services were provided temporarily throughout the inspection and search operation to ensure passengers could continue their journeys safely.

items.title: MOH says mask up, avoid outdoor activity as haze blankets Malaysia with unhealthy air
items.summary: The Ministry of Health (MOH) said that if N95 face masks are unavailable, the use of three-ply face masks can be considered as a limited additional protection measure. According to MOH, wearing appropriate face masks is crucial to reduce exposure to air pollutants, especially when the Air Pollutant Index (API) reading exceeds 100, which is at an unhealthy level. “However, if it is necessary to conduct activities outdoors, the public is advised to use appropriate face masks,” according to the statement yesterday.

items.title: AKPS officer allegedly killed by husband was in divorce proceedings, says brother
items.summary: According to Sinar Harian , Amran Ibrahim, 59, said he initially could not believe the news that his youngest sister, Norhazwani Ibrahim, 35, had been stabbed to death, allegedly by her husband. He said he received a call from another brother at about 7.30pm yesterday informing him that Norhazwani had been killed and that her husband had surrendered to police. Amran said he then contacted the police station, which confirmed that his sister had died after being stabbed.

items.title: Pending assemblyman hints Sarawak election may fall on Dec 12 or Dec 19
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 16 — Pending assemblyman Violet Yong believes the next Sarawak election will be held either on December 12 or December 19, this year. She made the remarks when concluding her debate speech on the State Budget 2027 at the State Legislative Assembly (DUN) sitting today. The term of the 19th State Legislative Assembly will expire in February next year.

items.title: Tuition teacher held over alleged sexual offences involving five male students in Bukit Jalil
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 16 — A tuition teacher has been arrested over alleged sexual offences involving five male students with police investigating separate reports involving teenage and child victims, the New Straits Times reported. City police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said the alleged offences took place at the suspect’s home, which was also used as a tuition centre. According to the English daily, he said five police reports had been lodged at the Bukit Jalil police station, with the first made on October 6, followed by another on October 10 and three more on October 11.

items.title: Pan Borneo Sabah delays stem from multiple factors, not one party, says projects chief inspector
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Oct 16 — Delays in the Pan Borneo Sabah Highway Phase 1A project cannot be attributed to any single party, with technical, administrative and financial challenges all contributing to the slow pace of implementation, said Datuk Seri Salleh Mohd Said Keruak. The Chief Inspector of Projects Sabah said it was unfair to place the entire blame on the Sabah government, stressing that the completion of the long-awaited highway required closer cooperation among all parties involved. He said lengthy approval processes had also affected the smooth implementation of the project.
